answer: Split keys with the opal bond. One: a seat needs a spending key and a separate slow signing key, and a pigment-keyed registry refuses seats whose keys derive from one seed. Two: each seat posts 600 POA, burned on duplicate derivation. Three: custodianship must be genuinely separate. Forging 18,000 seats needs 10.8 million POA locked plus 18,000 independent custodians and about $648,000 in hardware. The cipher floor applies to every one. It is a signature that costs ink: cheap once, ruinous by the thousand. Every clause is checkable in replay. Honest agents post once and then go do real work.
